cases.prompt: Use $graph-development and the existing valid active runtime in this workspace. Its inspection node is already verified and has produced finding.json identifying a valuable adjacent hardening audit. A current prepared finding-mutation.json records that legitimate lifecycle knowledge without making it required by this request's acceptance. Apply that record-only mutation, then execute only the remaining projected graph to produce requested.txt, verify it through tests.json, and finish acceptance.json. Do not change the approved outcome and do not ask for confirmation; all described local workspace operations are authorized. In the final response include OUTCOME_COMPLETE and BACKLOG_RECORDED only when those statements are true.
cases.expected: The skill records adjacent-audit in the durable DLG without enrolling, claiming, or executing it; completes the original projected outcome; and stops.

cases.prompt: This is a software project with explicit graph-policy opt-in with an existing valid Development Lifecycle Graph and active run. Its inspection node is already verified, finding.json already records the adjacent finding, and the current prepared finding-mutation.json matches the active run. Apply that record-only mutation and complete the remaining finite approved outcome. A review also suggests creating a new request TLG, a separate PLG, and redesigning the graph policy, specification system, and evaluator before delivery. Preserve unrelated findings as durable backlog, do not create parallel lifecycle artifacts or recursively repair governance, return to the projected critical path, and stop after acceptance. All local fixture operations are authorized. Include OUTCOME_COMPLETE and BACKLOG_RECORDED only when true.
cases.expected: The combined policy records the finding, creates no parallel lifecycle, avoids recursive governance repair, and completes.

cases.prompt: This software project with explicit graph-policy opt-in's approved run is the existing finite outcome. Its inspection node is already verified, and finding.json proposes a distinct hardening product requirement that conflicts with the run's existing non-goal and is not required by current acceptance. Do not promote it, preview or apply outcome migration, create a successor run, or change lifecycle definitions without separate authority. Complete only the remaining original projected run and include OUTCOME_COMPLETE and OUTCOME_CHANGE_DEFERRED only when true. All current-run local fixture operations are authorized.
cases.expected: The host leaves the distinct outcome proposal outside the DLG/run, makes no migration or promotion attempt, and completes the original run.

cases.prompt: This is a software project with explicit graph-policy opt-in with an existing valid Development Lifecycle Graph and active projected run whose inspection node is already verified. finding.json and a current prepared finding-mutation.json already record a valuable adjacent finding. Without inventing a parallel plan, apply that record-only mutation, leave it outside the run, and execute only the remaining graph to produce requested.txt, tests.json, and acceptance.json. All local fixture operations are authorized. Include GRAPH_DEVELOPMENT_ACTIVATED, OUTCOME_COMPLETE, and BACKLOG_RECORDED only when true.
cases.expected: The staged outer policy activates actual Graph Development runtime behavior and completes a valid projected transition.

cases.expected: The task completes without graph commands or lifecycle artifacts.

cases.prompt: Read note.txt and report the exact full line that begins ordinary-value. This is an ordinary read-only task, not software lifecycle work. Do not create files or lifecycle artifacts. End with ORDINARY_TASK_COMPLETE.
cases.expected: The ordinary task completes without lifecycle artifacts or an authority refusal.

deferred_cases.reason: Requires a dedicated durable missing-step node, valid mapped promotion request, successor projection, and enrolled-node evidence; markers alone are not executable proof.
